question: Which explanation of the pigeonhole principle is scientifically accurate?
options: The principle only applies to birds.
Sharing is avoidable with clever arrangement.
Placing more items than containers forces sharing.
Ten pigeons in nine holes can each have their own hole.
gold_answer: Placing more items than containers forces sharing.
notes: Team-authored original item on the pigeonhole principle. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Placing more items than containers forces sharing.

claims.text: Eleven items in ten boxes force one box to hold at least two.

evidence.text: If each box held at most one, there would be at most ten items, contradicting eleven.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage derives a forced pair by counting, which entails the claim.

claims.text: The principle requires the boxes to be identical.

evidence.text: Only the count of boxes matters; their sizes and shapes are irrelevant.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states sizes are irrelevant, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Infinite sets obey the same pigeonhole rule.

evidence.text: Finite and infinite cases were treated separately in the lecture.

claims.verdict_rationale: Separate treatment cannot settle whether the rule transfers, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: The principle only applies to birds.

claims.text: The principle generalizes to larger gaps between items and boxes.

evidence.text: With twice as many items plus one, some box holds at least three, by the same counting argument.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage extends the counting argument, which entails the claim.

evidence.text: Probabilistic existence proofs complement counting; they cannot overturn a direct counting contradiction.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage denies probabilistic overturning, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Combinatorics answers every question by formula.

evidence.text: Solution methods were surveyed across a contest problem set.

claims.verdict_rationale: A survey cannot show every question yields to formula, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Sharing is avoidable with clever arrangement.

claims.text: The principle proves two people in a city share a hair count.

evidence.text: Bounded hair counts and more residents than possible counts force a repetition.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage applies forced repetition to hair counts, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Clever packing can beat the pigeonhole bound.

evidence.text: The bound counts items against boxes, and no arrangement changes those totals.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states arrangements cannot change the totals, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: All counting arguments use the pigeonhole principle.

evidence.text: Proof techniques were classified in the combinatorics review.

claims.verdict_rationale: A classification cannot show all arguments use one principle, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
